title: Who CAN and CANNOT Be On Title When you Get A Mortgage?
h2: Can you add your spouse to the title?

Are you in a community property state?

We suggest speaking with an attorney when dealing with any transfer of title
Transcript of the Mortgage Brothers Podcast

faqs.q: Who CAN and CANNOT Be On Title When You Get A Mortgage?
faqs.a: Of course you can. If you’re getting a mortgage, you can absolutely add your spouse to the title.

faqs.q: Can your spouse be on the title even if they’re not on the mortgage?
faqs.a: You can have your spouse on the title even if they’re not on the mortgage. However, if they’re on the mortgage, if they’re on the loan, they have to be on the title because you have to have rights to the home in order to encumber the home by getting a loan on it. This is true for any co-borrower, even if it’s not your spouse.

faqs.q: Are you in a community property state?
faqs.a: This is another thing that’s good to be aware of. If you’re in a community property state this means that if your spouse dies and you’re not on the title then the house would go to you. Arizona, for example, is a community state property.
